events.title: Justinian dedicates Hagia Sophia
events.description: Emperor Justinian dedicated the new church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, built in under six years. It was the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years and later served as a mosque and a museum.

events.title: The Zwickau prophets arrive in Wittenberg
events.description: Three men of the Radical Reformation, exiled from Zwickau, arrived in Wittenberg, where their ideas won favour with Andreas Karlstadt and others. The unrest that followed brought Martin Luther back from protective custody at the Wartburg in March 1522.

events.title: The Swedes lift their siege of the Jasna Góra Monastery
events.description: With their position in southern Lesser Poland deteriorating, the Swedish invaders lifted their siege of the Pauline monastery of Jasna Góra in Częstochowa, home of the Black Madonna icon. The defence galvanised Polish resistance and made the monastery a national symbol.

events.title: Residents of Flushing sign the Flushing Remonstrance
events.description: Some thirty residents of Flushing in New Netherland, none of them Quakers, signed a petition asking Director-General Peter Stuyvesant to exempt them from his ban on Quaker worship. It is considered a precursor of religious freedom in the Bill of Rights.

events.title: The schooner USS Carolina is destroyed, ending Patterson's makeshift fleet
events.description: The destruction of the schooner USS Carolina ended Commodore Daniel Patterson's makeshift fleet, whose delaying actions contributed to Andrew Jackson's victory over the British at New Orleans in 1815.

events.title: HMS Beagle sails with Charles Darwin aboard
events.description: HMS Beagle left Plymouth on a surveying voyage with the 22-year-old naturalist Charles Darwin. His observations over the five-year journey shaped his later theory of evolution.
events.html: HMS Beagle left Plymouth on a surveying voyage with the 22-year-old naturalist Charles Darwin. His observations over the five-year journey shaped his later theory of evolution.

events.title: Peter Pan opens on the London stage
events.description: J. M. Barrie's play Peter Pan, or the Boy Who Wouldn't Grow Up opened at the Duke of York's Theatre. Its story of Neverland, Captain Hook and Tinker Bell became a children's classic.
events.html: J. M. Barrie's play Peter Pan, or the Boy Who Wouldn't Grow Up opened at the Duke of York's Theatre. Its story of Neverland, Captain Hook and Tinker Bell became a children's classic.

events.title: Soviet special forces kill Afghanistan's leader Hafizullah Amin
events.description: As Soviet troops poured into Afghanistan, commandos stormed the Tajbeg Palace in Kabul and killed President Amin. The decade-long war that followed cost hundreds of thousands of Afghan lives.
